topics.title: Question in Euler's totient function
topics.text:
To derive the formula, let us first define the prime factorization of $n$ as $n =\prod_{i=1}^{m}p_i^{e_i} =p_1^{e_1}p_2^{e_2}\cdots p_m^{e_m}$ where the $p_i$ are distinct prime numbers. Now, we can use a PIE argument to count the number of numbers less than or equal to  $n$ that are relatively prime to it.



First, let's count the complement of what we want (i.e. all the numbers less than or equal to $n$ that share a common factor with it). There are $\frac{n}{p_1}$ positive integers less than or equal to $n$ that are divisible by $p_1$



My question is :

if $n = p_1^{e_1}p_2^{e_2}\cdots p_m^{e_m}$ divided by ${p_1}$, then how come $\frac{n}{p_1}$ isdivisible by $p_1$ if already divided?.

Because the factor ${p_1}$ aleady gone in $n$, then it's co-prime with $n$ right ?. Can some please calrify this question ?

topics.title: k My Math Career So Far and I need help
topics.text:
Hey guys!

It's your boy (actually, this probably isn't true, I'm rarely active on community)

So I saw a couple of incredible posts today, and I decided to create my own! Right into it:

My Math Career So Far And I need helpI began mathematics as a 4th grader trying to have fun. I know that sounds strange, but my parents did constantly force me to study, so I chose math. A simple subject where you're so smart because you memorized the 9x9 table. At least that's how I envisioned it. I was quite the person to talk to back then.

I think what really humbled me was a competition I attended that year. (I don't specifically recall the name)

I didn't expect to do well on it, I expected to get 1st. I was so confident that I was a stellar math student. (Once again, this is the younger, former self of me)



I ended up placing... well I didn't place. That's how bad I did.

The winner was a math prodigy named Jake ____ (I will leave out the last name because of privacy)

Apparently his father was one of the math competition problem writers, and his mother was a tutor for gifted math students.



Anyway, I wasn't feeling too good. Neither were my parents. They decided that I should study more often, more than the meager 30 minutes I did back then. They made me watch a bunch of videos done by famous Korean math teachers that weren't fun but weren't exactly boring. I did it because I didn't want to fail, so to speak.

The next year, the school started an afterschool math club. I was one of the top students there, (even though I was pretty bad back then) enough that people often came to me for help, and I was a role model.

The next competition arrived, and I really didn't care about it. I did try my best, but I told myself that if I didn't place, I was perfectly OK.



I did place, I recall it being 13th in the region. (Note: This is not Mathcounts) It wasn't too bad, it was better than I had expected.



And, of course, Jake won.



Then I was introduced to AoPS.



My brother had a friend who did AoPS (who later made Nats from Florida) and that friend introduced him to it. He showed the FTW! part of the resources given. My brother constantly played on that, and I decided to do it as well. I made my AoPS account and played with people. I made some "friends" that I didn't know, and I eventually got up to the rating of... 903.



So I didn't really care at the moment. I still don't. But I looked at that score, and I thought, 'Wow'



A former student who thought was a great math student couldn't even go above average for some math website. It was at this point that I fueled my effort into math.

I came home running and played FTW! for around 2 hours a day, doing homework, then practicing golf, going to sleep. That was the daily routine.



Eventually, another opportunity came for another math competition (Gosh darn it, I forgot the name...)

I went there with my mother's friend and her daughter who also participated.

I ended up getting 1st, beating Jake. This was unexpected, as I hadn't done any learning. All I had done was bash FTW! questions. But what made me mad was that my parents weren't there. I know that sounds strange, because they are going to know that you got first. You have your award as proof. But at the moment, I realized how little confidence my parents had in me. They could have gone to the competition. There was no schedule in between, or anything that clashed with time. They just didn't want to go.



The next year, I moved to Connecticut.



I began learning about Mathcounts as the school started and progressed. Eventually I had the school round, which I placed 10th. From there, chapter round came, and I scored ok. Not good at all compared to some of the posters I have seen, but 33 isn't too bad. I then qualified for states. I studied quite ferociously for the state round, and after hearing that the top 4 make it to Nationals, I wanted to be one of them. Then the day for the competition arrived. During the contest, I tried my best, but the moment I saw question 10 on sprint, I gave up. The questions were just too hard. I failed states miserably, placing in the 60's. It was at this point that I realized, 'Whoa. Wait a minute. I thought I was good at math. I beat a math prodigy. I got 3rd in my chapter. And all I amount to is a lowly 60th place? All that work for a score of 20?"



I wasn't very happy. It was very hard to look at that score and think that I was even decent at math. It was at this moment, that I realized that I wasn't good at math. Connecticut itself isn't a very good state for mathematics. (sorry!)

Yet I still only got 60th place? I decided that I was going to go Nats.

Next year, same routine happened. I ended up getting tied for 2nd with 2 others for school round. I scored a lowly 37, however, we were not allowed to use calculators because the coach didn't like them, blah blah. Then in chapter, I scored a 38, placing 7th this time, but getting 3rd in countdown. It was this point that my self esteem dropped. There was another school that just joined Mathcounts, East Lyme. I met some new people who also did AoPS. I think that I am allowed to say their usernames so I will. They are well-known members in the community: Ultroid999OCPN and Aditya11. I became quick friends with them (but I prefer to bug them) Aditya and Ultroid both placed in top 8 making countdown, with Ultroid getting 1st.



For states, I was sure I was going to place in nationals. Except I didn't. I placed so bad that it was in the triple digits, much worse than last year, which made no sense to me. How could I drop ranking after a year of work? Not even that, my score itself dropped as well. When I came home, I decided to lie to my parents, saying I placed 38th, so I wouldn't get in trouble. They still don't know to this day.



They congratulated me on my "score" and told me I could make Nats. You'd probably expect me to feel bad. And I did. I felt so bad that I even fell into depression, but I didn't tell anyone else. I wasn't depressed enough to consider suicide, but still, it was serious. My reasoning was that I was a kid who had absolutely no talent at all, I just had a lot of time and used it on math, and that was why I did slightly better than average. I wasn't superb in other classes. Sure, my grades were stereoypically all A's, but I didn't feel smart at all.

Next year (AKA this year. Things get really bad here)



In school I got another 37. I wasn't at all surprised, the test was harder and I made sillies. Not to mention the fact that we weren't allowed to use calculators. Well I just did. Oh well. I placed 1st in countdown. Chapter, I scored a 42. Although this is a reasonably ok score, (I'm not lying here->)  I almost decided not to participate in countdown. I had sillied two question that I could have easily done in my sleep. One was aprint number x# where you had to find the amount of rectangles in a rectangle - I forgot to add correctly, thinking apparently that 30+6 was 30. Then on target, I didn't realize that 4^6 was 4096 and got 3096. I didn't realize that 4^6 was a power of 2 and that 4096 was a power of two and ironically that 4096 and 3096 were very close in number comparison. Not even that, I could have used a calculator on it realize that I was computing wrong. I was so enraged at this. Countdown? I choked because of thinking about that, losing to a 6th grader (no offense) There's your answer, Ultroid and Aditya, why I didn't do well in countdown. Because I didn't want to do the questions. I let him win.



States. I bashed my brain out for this competition. This was it. The last year for Mathcounts. I couldn't put anything together, and I couldn't reason my score for sprint. Target, I got all but 2, getting a 12. As the names for countdown were being called, I was sweating all over the place. So sweaty that my shoes had to be washed because of how much water was down there. I didn't go to countdown. It was very... expected yet disappointing. I later got my score:24. I placed 42th (Yay, the meaning of life, the universe, and everything) I came home and told my parents my score, and they weren't happy at all. I still hadn't told them that I placed close to 100th last year in states, and they still don't know. It was this time that I took some time off. I always began thinking about my entire life, and what I had amounted to. I became so depressed that my grades dropped and I even began thinking of suicide (ok, don't freak out, I'm not dead right now, I don't consider it as much). Basically, I had sacrificed my entire life to a field of academics, only to amount to a lowly score. This was the reason why I had such few friends, with little social status, no social skills, why I was called an "offie." My brother was better than me. He went to national science bowl twice, he placed 47th in Mathcounts without even trying or studying at all, he won the school scholar award, which is a huge thing. He excelled in his classes. He's super popular, better looking than me. To make things worse, he treats me a like a dog. To quote him, "The younger one gets no rights. The older one can do anything and there is nothing the younger one can do." Whenever my mom and dad were out, he would make me do everything. Cleaning, making lunch, etc... If I objected, he would hit me or punch me. I still have bruises on my face. He still is like this.

I didn't receive the scholar award. I didn't make Nationals in any subjects. I don't have many friends. My grades aren't good.



I even look at my friends. BrainHu25? He's in calculus. I'm in pre-calculus, and we're in the same grade. AsianFatPanda? His grades are better than mine. Ultroid? He got double tie blocked in states, getting 5th. At least he placed. Aditya? He qualified for AIME.



I'll put it on a larger scale.

Connecticut is an average state. Yet in my school alone, there are so many people who are smarter than me. Yet there are states that have people smarter than them, and so forth. It just says to me, ProGameXD, you aren't smart.



You're one of 7.1 billion people on this earth.



And you're nowhere near number one.



I'm a failure.



My feelings have decreased in severity after a couple months with the shenanigans, but my feelings still are negative. I need help.



The conclusion: I understand that this story is a darker one, not like the inspirational ones. My takeaway from this is that Life Won't Go Your Way. I know that's strange, how that even ties in with the story, but I've learned that you can't always expect good results. It'll just get your hopes high, and if you don't do good, you'll feel worse. That being said, DO try that competition. DO try that new skill or activity. DO try. Because of you don't, there is no way to do it.



I'm trying to be as realistic as possible right now. Practicing really does make a difference. But you won't always get the results you need, or you want. Fate is cruel that way. But it's also good that way.



Thanks for reading.


Ok guys, I'm just asking for help. Seriously

topics.title: k Mathcounts Marathon
topics.text:
I would like to start a Mathcounts Marathon.  Here are the rules:



[list]

[*]Please number your problems and solutions so that people will know which problem/solution you are referring to.

[*]Please use the "hide" tags for your problems and solutions like this:

*(Please note the quotes around the Problem/Solution Title, they are mandatory.)

[code]Problem/Solution Title with Number.Problem/Solution goes here
[/code]

[*]I will post the first problem.  Then someone else can post a full solution to my problem (remember to use the "hide" tags and numbering!) in addition to posting a new problem. You may use an old Mathcounts question as long as you provide its location (e.x: 2013 State Sprint #23). If you don't have a new problem, you can always use Google!  But make sure to cite the source you used to get the problem.  :)

[*]Why is it important to useYou should use the "hide" tags so that people won't have to have the solutions staring at them right in the face.  When the solution is easily accessible, people will have a tendency to look at it right away if they can't do the problem on the first try, and if you do that, you aren't learning at all.



Additionally, you should also number your problems so that referencing different problems can be much less problematic.




[*]***IMPORTANT***

Above all, remember the level of this marathon, this is the Math counts Marathon so try not to make the name of this Marathon start deceiving others. Anyways, just remember to keep the problems at a $\text{Math counts}$ level but the problems can (and should) challenge the scholars in this community.[/list]



With that said, I would like to thank JSGandora for the formatting of the rules (I made some minor edits, and thus did not insert quotations).



Here's the first problem: Source: December 21, 2015 Math counts problem of the week 

Problem 1Speedy Delivery charges 20 dollars to send a 1-pound package via two-day service and an additional 2 dollars for every 4 ounces of package weight over 1 pound. How much will it cost to ship a package that weighs 3.75 pounds via Speedy Delivery’s two-day service?

topics.title: k Problems with clogging up the forum
topics.text:
Recently, over the past couple of weeks, I've seen a bunch of math marathons, and other silly math games being posted. These spammy actions are clogging up the forum. Posting in a copy marathon: "Ughh another marathon" actually spams it more! I'm going to dive deeper in reasons why people do things like this, and how to remove them. I have some experience, as I used to do this.



Before you read on, this is where all of the marathons went.

------------

1. They need more attention.



This one is not very common, so I'm going to get it out of the way first. If a user is new, and doesn't get what the community is for, he/she will start posting polls and marathons to catch attention, or to get upvotes...



2. Upvotes.



Upon seeing successful marathons like the 24 math game, people will want to get upvotes. (By the way, the 24 game is >50 upvotes, so it will be natural to do this)



3. Ignorance.



I'm hoping this is the most common. Some people might not even know that they shouldn't post them! In this case, a nice PM or post should be fine.



4. Pure trolls. :mad:



Now these are the types of people that post to



i. Get attention

ii. Be mean

iii. Clog up the forum



We need to report these types of posts. :!:

-------------

How to fix these problems:



If you know a user that is nice, never trolls, and starts posting these polls on MSM, then PM them, and ask them why they did this. If you don't know them, and it is one of their first posts, then they either will be new/ignorant, or they are multis/trolls. If you realize the person knows an awful amount of AoPS forums, he/she might be a multi account, but don't conclude yet. We want to give new users a chance! If a new user makes a silly poll, PM the user first. If they are a troll, report the topic.



Now you might say, "What if the marathon is good?"



Well yes, I have seen a couple of good ones. If you have a solid idea, keep it in your head, then ask around the community if it is a good idea. This will help you to not spam. Please do not spam by asking people.



Another thing that is clogging MSM is the absurd amount of Alcumus problems. What's the point of asking alcumus in MSM? To get the answer right? Go to the Alcumus forum! There's already one there! Make sure you use Gamebot though!



If you don't have time to read through this whole post, read this summary:



SummaryThere are many ways to clog the forum. From posting Alcumus to polls, please refrain from doing this.



If you see spam,



i. If the user is a known troll, report.

ii. If the user is new, tell the user.



Please, older users of AoPS, please be a good example to the younger users. Instead of saying, "Ughh another marathon," say, "Please stop spamming the forum" or, "Please refrain from posting alcumus questions in Middle school math".




AND...



Please no advertising in Middle school math, high school math, high school olympiads, and I could go on and on.Happycupcake and GCampos don't criticize me for advertising please. :P




Thanks for helping to "un-clog" the forum on the very best website in the world! :D



~lakecomo224
